pages.contentHtml:
We are the McMaster Marching Band

Thank you to Maya Tsipris for this amazing video of The McMaster Marching Band!
The McMaster Marching Band (MMB) established in 2009, is one of few university marching bands in Canada. Composed of hornline, drumline, and colour guard, MMB is proud to showcase the musical talents of students studying at McMaster in a unique and fun way. 

MMB is active on campus and endeavours to embody school spirit at varsity games, in addition to special events in collaboration with the McMaster Students Union (M﻿﻿SU) and other University organizations. The Band also bridges the gap between McMaster University and the Hamilton community, performing at various local events including the annual Hamilton Santa Claus Parade.

As a band, we have been asked to perform at a number of high-profile performances such as the Toronto Santa Claus Parade, the largest Christmas Parade around the world viewed by more than one million people every year. Most notably, the MMB has performed alongside Serena Ryder in the ET Canada New Year's Eve Bash 2014 (televised nationally), during the Toronto Raptors Holiday Halftime Show 2017, and took part in the filming of the IT Chapter II movie.

pages.contentHtml:
Want to sign up for the 2025-2026 school year? Fill out the form!

Fill out the form! Join the Discord server

Interested?

We accept members year round! If you're interested in learning more about us or joining the band, fill out the Google form!
No experience? No worries! We provide all members with an instrument or flag plus music instruction, free!
Rehearsals are drop-in, so you can come try!
 

Rehearsal Location & Time

We rehearse Tuesdays 7:30-10:00 PM in
Fitzhenry Studio @ David Braley Athletic Centre (DBAC)
1280 Main St West
Hamilton, ON, L8S 4E8
Take the elevator at the back of the lower level to the 2nd floor and follow the track to the right.

New members attending their first rehearsal should arrive 30 minutes early to grab an instrument and get set up.

Our ensemble﻿

MMB has a hornline (brass, woodwinds), drumline and colour guard! You can join any of these groups, no experience required! We can provide instruments and instruction to those who need it. Interested in learning more? Fill out the form and check out our groups below.  Any questions, feel free to fill out the form!

Brass

MMB's brass section consists of brass instruments including trumpets, trombones, sousaphones and more. They provide the sing-along melody and the thumping bass lines to all our tunes.

Woodwinds

MMB's woodwinds consist of woodwind instruments including flutes, clarinets, saxophones and more.

Drumline

The drumline is the heartbeat of MMB. While they play alongside the rest of the band, they also show of their repertoire of street beats. The drumline consists of snare drums, bass drums, tenor drums, and cymbals.

Colour Guard

The colour guard leads the band, spinning flags and dancing spectacular choreography to the music. There is no dance experience needed to join the team.

pages.contentHtml:
FAQ

StudentsOrganizers
 

FAQ for Students

1. What does a marching band do exactly?

We perform at a ton of events throughout the school year. Every year we'll play Santa Claus Parades and varsity sports games, as well as other events that come our way, such as Toronto Raptors Half-Time shows or a New Year's Eve Concert with Serena Ryder.

2. How much are membership fees? 

There is no annual membership fee! All members are required to pay a one-time $40 fee and a $100 deposit for insurance, but the fee can be returned if you decide not to join. The insurance is also returned to you at the end of the year provided that your assigned uniform and instrument is undamaged.

3. Do I have to bring my own instrument? 

No! MMB has a wide variety of brass, woodwind, and percussion instruments that are free for our members.

4. Do I have to pay for my uniform? 

Nope! MMB has uniforms of all sizes and you'll be assigned a full set before your first event.

5. When are rehearsals?

 MMB meets Tuesdays 7:30-10:00 PM in Fitzhenry Studio, David Braley Athletic Centre (DBAC). More information can be found on our join page.
6. I have another question!
We'd love to hear it – drop us a line and we'll get back to you!
 

FAQ for Event Organizers

1. Can we hire MMB for an event?
To get the ball rolling to hire MMB, get in touch with your event details!
2. How much does hiring MMB cost?
It depends based on the event, date, and location. Drop us a line and we can provide a quote.
3. How many performers do you have?
We typically perform with 40+ musicians. If you have a specific headcount in mind, let us know and we'd be happy to explore the possibilities with you!

pages.bannerHtml: Our Team
pages.contentHtml:
Executives

Sifan Liu ​(she/her)

Administrative Director, Percussion
Honours Health Sciences II
Sifan is MMB's administrative director, in charge of all the day-to-day operations for the band like planning rehearsals, organising events, and recruitment. Sifan started in band as a percussionist and now continues as a proud member of the drumline.

Airo Marsh ​(he/they)

Operations Director, Percussion
Level IV Arts & Science
Airo is ecstatic to be this year's Operations Director, responsible for bus bookings, band accessibility, administrative logistics, and other behind the scenes work! He plays the bass drum and is committed to further enhancing MMB’s supportive environment! Outside of band, you can find Airo dancing, climbing, or existentialising about an unexamined life.​

Samara Rahman (she/her)

Communications Director, Flute
Honours Health Sciences III 
As Communications Director, Samara is responsible for managing event sign up forms, calendars, rehearsal announcements, as well as all other internal and external communications between general members, execs, alumni, and staff. She is your primary source of information on the MMB discord. Outside of marching band, she likes to draw and play video games.

Norah Morrison ​(she/her)

Finance Director, Flute
Actuarial and Financial Mathematics II
Norah is super excited to serve as this year’s Finance Director! In this role, she manages the band’s budget, tracks expenses, and somehow makes sense of all the numbers behind the scenes. This is her second year marching with the band, and she brings over six years of flute-playing experience to the ensemble. Outside of band, Norah is also a proud enthusiast of “grandma” hobbies and her porch goose!
​

Alaine Hibbert (she/her)

Promotions Director, Flute
Honours Molecular Biology & Genetics III
Alaine brings creativity, energy, and a genuine love for the band to her work in promotions. She plans to find new ways to showcase the band’s story, celebrate its members, and build excitement around events this year!! When she’s not at band, you can find her studying for her upcoming biology test. ❤️

Oie Mok (any)

Social Director, Percussion + Flags
Materials Engineering III
As your Social Director, not only bringing snacks and hyping up every event, Oie will make sure everyone enjoys their time vibing with each other in the band! Outside of work, Oie loves anime and games, sometimes sketching or randomly go on exploring secret paths on campus.

Mia Tran​ (she/her)

Logistics Director, Saxophone
Integrated Sciences (Psychology, Neuroscience and Behaviour) II
Mia is the Logistics Director and manages everything relating to inventory, instruments, and uniforms! She also comes with an alarming amount of unexplained lore, a soft spot for every animal she meets, and a tendency to disappear on spontaneous adventures that somehow escalate far beyond the original plan.

Richard Hull (he/him)

Music Educational Director, Saxophone
Richard's involvement with the McMaster Marching Band began two years ago and was appointed Musical Director in 2023. Richard has been teaching instrumental music at the middle school level with the Halton District School Board since 2006 and is a member of the Ontario College of Teachers, the Ontario Band Association, and the Ontario Music Educators’ Association. Outside of teaching, directing, and performing with various bands, he maintains an active family focused lifestyle that includes walking his dogs and canoeing.

MaySon Scanlan ​(he/him)

Assistant Director/Drill Instructor, Trumpet
MaySon is a seasoned trumpet player with over 20 years of experience, from Drum Corps International (DCI) to British Brass Bands. Currently, he marches with the Canadian Armed Forces and has performed for heads of state and royalty, specializing in marching music. MaySon also teaches Drill and Marching for Gayly Forward, Canada’s most inclusive LGTBQ+ marching band.

Cole

Liam Henderson

Guard lead

To be announced
